newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond volatilities softer,await auctions.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond volatilities softer,await auctions.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were mostly softer in quiet trading as the market awaited the Treasury's refunding auctions later this week, dealers said.

With underlying bond prices drifting narrowly mixed in slow trading and the market's attention focused on broader portfolio management ahead of the auctions, options activity seemed confined to position adjustments, they said.
"You probably are not going to see a whole lot of volume in options this week," a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade said.
The U.S. Treasury is to auction $17.75 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday, $12 billion in 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
"You might see some hedging, but so far today we haven't seen any big initiating positions," the brokerage trader said.

Implied volatility for CBOT March T-bond futures options stood at 8.2 percent, off half a point from late Friday levels. With only two weeks of life to expiration, implied volatility for the March contract was fluctuating widely relative to the rest of the market and heavily influenced by time element, traders said.
Implied volatility for June T-bond futures options was virtually unchanged from Friday at around 9.65 percent, after blipping up by about 0.1 point in early trade.

Among the largest trades in the CBOT pit, an investment bank was said to have sold 2,000 contracts of March 110 puts. The bank had bought some 5,000 of the same contract late last week prior to Friday's January employment report and was seen getting out of that position.
Another firm was seen buying 2,000 contracts of March 114 calls and a third firm buying 1,000 March 113 calls.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were generally steady to marginally softer.
"We opened softer and were better offered all day," a brokerage trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. He added, however, that buying on dips supported volatilities.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options stood at 9.8 and 12.9 percent respectively.
Traders said foreign exchange rates after the weekend Group of Seven meeting was a source of concern but that the dollar seemed to have maintained its bullish bias so far.

Apart from the Treasury auctions, the biggest events for interest rate markets foreseeable this week are probably Thursday's January retail sales and Friday's producer prices data. But traders said they expected little spark from those numbers after coming through last week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and January employment report without major turbulence.
